# Old format of Fude Polygon data

The Fude Polygon data published by MAFF on <https://open.fude.maff.go.jp> for the years 2021 and 2022 is in GeoJSON format. 
These datasets include local government codes but lack the `key` column, which identifies geographical locations such as municipalities or communities. 
Relying solely on the 6-digit local government codes (the `local_government_cd` column) can be confusing, as most users are not familiar with them. 
Therefore, this package aims to enhance user-friendliness by converting these numeric codes into readable Japanese geographical names.

```{r echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
library(fude)

d0 <- read_fude("~/2022_38.zip", quiet = TRUE)
names(d0)
names(d0[[1]])
```

## List the contents of Fude Polygon data

```{r}
ls_fude(d0)
```

## Rename the local government code

**Note:** This feature is available only for data obtained from GeoJSON.

You can convert local government codes into Japanese municipality names for easier data management.
```{r}
d1 <- rename_fude(d0)
names(d1)
```

You can also rename the columns to Romaji instead of Japanese.
```{r}
d2 <- d0 |>
  rename_fude(suffix = TRUE, romaji = "title", quiet = FALSE)
```

# New format of Fude Polygon data

Since 2024, the Fude Polygon data published by MAFF <https://www.maff.go.jp/j/tokei/census/shuraku_data/2025/mb/> is provided in FlatGeobuf format.
This new format includes a `key` column that identifies municipalities and communities.
However, it does not include the corresponding Japanese geographical names.
Because the `key` is merely a 10-digit number, users cannot intuitively identify locations without mapping them to proper Japanese names.

```{r echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
dn <- read_fude("~/MB0001_2026_2025_38.zip.001", quiet = TRUE)
names(dn)
names(dn[[1]])
```

## List the contents of Fude Polygon data

```{r}
ls_fude(dn)
```

## Combination with agricultural community boundaries

Combining Fude Polygons with agricultural community boundary data provides deeper geographical insights and makes the data much easier to work with.

```{r echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
b <- get_boundary(d0, path = "~", quiet = TRUE)
b

db <- d0 |>
  lapply(sf::st_transform, crs = sf::st_crs(b[[1]])) |>
  combine_fude(b, city = "松山市", rcom = "由良|北浦|鷲ケ巣|門田|馬磯|泊|御手洗|船越")
db

dbn <- combine_fude(dn, b, city = "松山市", rcom = "由良|北浦|鷲ケ巣|門田|馬磯|泊|御手洗|船越")
dbn
```
